prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1081; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from the insured by phone. Insured reports a collision at an intersection while making a left turn. Other vehicle was traveling straight through on the opposing approach. No injuries reported by insured at time of call. Assigned file to adjuster and requested photos, police report number, and recorded statement.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured for recorded statement. Insured states the light was green for their left turn and the opposing vehicle appeared to be speeding. Insured says the impact was to the driver's side front quarter panel of the insured vehicle. Insured did not mention any head injury during this call. Obtained copy of the police report, which lists the other driver as cited for failure to yield on a left turn, though the report narrative is still being reviewed.

Entry 3: Contact received from the claimant's attorney's office. Claimant is represented and all further communication must go through counsel. Attorney advises that claimant was diagnosed with a concussion at the emergency department following the collision and is under ongoing care. Requested medical authorization forms and a copy of the emergency department records. Placed a hold on any direct contact with the claimant.

Entry 4: Reviewed photos and vehicle damage estimate for the insured vehicle. Damage consistent with the reported angle of impact. Received liability position from the other carrier disputing fault and asserting the insured turned without adequate clearance. Scheduled a scene reconstruction review and requested dash camera footage from both vehicles, if available.

Entry 5: Attorney's office sent records summary indicating claimant has been treated for post-concussive symptoms, including headaches and dizziness, and has missed work for a period of time. Bodily injury evaluation has been referred to the claims review unit. Noted that the file will remain open pending receipt of complete medical records and the outcome of the fault determination.
